# MarsDawn — full content

## MarsDawn

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/

Frontier tools for builders

# Claim the map. Read the dawn.

Markdown for humans who steer agentic work.

MarsDawn is a native Mac app for reading and reviewing Markdown, with live split preview, Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math, Quick Look and PDF export, free to try for 14 days and USD 4.99 once to unlock.

The page shows a working MarsDawn window over part of the app's Welcome guide. Its palette menu picks an appearance (System, Light, Dark) and a preview theme for light and for dark from four (Dawn, Classic, Modern, Vivid), and its toolbar one of three layouts (Source, Split, Preview).

## Read what your agent wrote.

1. **The agent writes.** Your coding agent or writing assistant drafts the Markdown: a README, a spec, a set of notes.
2. **You review in MarsDawn.** Open the file and read it rendered, with [Mermaid diagrams](/mermaid-preview-mac/) and highlighted code, next to the source.
3. **The agent revises.** Ask for changes. Open the revised file and read it the same way.

[How to review what your agent hands back](/reading-agent-output/) · [How to open a .md file on a Mac](/view-markdown-on-mac/)

## Review an agent's plan before it runs.

Catch the step that's out of order, point at its line, and hand it back.

1. See what changed: when the agent saves the plan, the open window updates from disk in one step you can undo.
2. Jump to the line: marsdawn open plan-checkout-v2.md:10 lands the window on line 10 and flashes the matching block.
3. Send it back: Copy Reference (⌥⌘C) copies plan-checkout-v2.md:10; paste it into the agent's chat with your note.

## Do this now

The free `marsdawn` command-line tool is ready today. Install it with Homebrew:

```
brew install redtear1115/tap/marsdawn
```

- `marsdawn export` turns a Markdown file into a PDF, rendered like MarsDawn's preview. It doesn't need the app.
- `marsdawn open` opens files in the MarsDawn app for you to review.
- `--json` gives scripts and agents results they can parse.

[Command Line](/cli/) · [marsdawn for agents](/cli/agents/) · [Agent skill](/cli/skill/) · [MCP server](/cli/mcp/)

## How the pieces fit

What each part does today, as of MarsDawn 1.1.1, marsdawn 0.6.4 and marsdawn-mcp v0.2.4.

| Capability | In the app | CLI | MCP / skill | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open at a line | Lands on the line, flashes the preview block | marsdawn open notes.md:120 (--background keeps focus) | open_in_marsdawn; the skill opens once | Shipped |
| PDF export | File ▸ Export as PDF… (⌥⌘E) | marsdawn export, no app needed | export_markdown_to_pdf; skill | Shipped |
| JSON result | — | --json on open and export | MCP returns the same JSON | Shipped |
| Agent skill | — | marsdawn skill --install | Teaches open once and export | Shipped |
| MCP server | — | Runs underneath | marsdawn-mcp: two tools, allowed folders only | Shipped |
| Copy for AI, Copy Reference | Edit ▸ Copy for AI (⌃⌥⌘C), Copy Reference (⌥⌘C) | — | — (paste into any agent) | Shipped |
| Live reload | Takes the saved change, one Undo | — | Skill: don't open again | Shipped |
| Claude Code hook | — | Uses open --background | Hook script from /cli/agents/ | Documented, opt-in |

Shipped: in the released version named above. Documented, opt-in: instructions on this site that you add yourself; not inside the tool. Planned: not built yet; no date. Planned: a folder option in the MCP open_in_marsdawn tool. More options, such as --folder, are on [Command Line](/cli/).

## If you build Mac apps with a coding agent

For indie Mac developers: how your agent can open what it wrote in MarsDawn today.

| Tool | How it pairs | Set up |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | The skill has it open what it wrote, once, at the line: `marsdawn open plan.md:42`. An opt-in hook opens each .md it writes, in the background | `marsdawn skill --install`; the hook script from /cli/agents/ |
| Codex, Cursor, Xcode | No setup guide yet. Anything that runs a shell command can call `marsdawn open file:line --json`; an agent that loads instruction files can use SKILL.md (`--dir`), and an MCP-only client can use marsdawn-mcp | `brew install redtear1115/tap/marsdawn` |

## Your documents stay on your Mac

On your Mac. Reading, editing, rendering, [PDF export](/privacy/#exporting-and-printing) and [the marsdawn command line](/privacy/#the-marsdawn-command-line-tool) all run here, offline; the app never uploads your documents.

More: [Privacy Policy](/privacy/#what-stays-on-your-mac)

Off the network by default. Web images load only when you click Load Images or turn on Load remote images automatically in Settings, and an HTML document opens static, with its code not run.

More: [Privacy Policy](/privacy/#when-marsdawn-uses-the-internet)

Leaves only when you choose. Copy for AI puts text on your clipboard for you to paste; a theme download, a document you run with View › Run This Document, and the agent you let read a file go out only on your say.

More: [Privacy Policy](/privacy/#when-marsdawn-uses-the-internet)

## Questions and answers

### What is MarsDawn?

MarsDawn is a native Mac app for reading and reviewing the Markdown your agent wrote, with the source beside a live preview. It draws Mermaid and KaTeX, previews .md files in Quick Look and exports PDF, and you can edit the source too.

### Is MarsDawn a subscription?

No. MarsDawn is a free download with a 14-day trial of every feature. After that, a single in-app purchase of USD 4.99 unlocks it for good. Nothing renews, and there is no account.

### Does MarsDawn work on iPhone or iPad?

No. MarsDawn is a Mac app and needs macOS 26 or later. There is no iPhone or iPad app.

### Can Claude Code open files in MarsDawn?

Yes. The free marsdawn command-line tool has an open command that opens a Markdown file in MarsDawn, so Claude Code, or any agent that can run a shell command, can call it. An opt-in Claude Code hook can open each Markdown file Claude writes or edits.

### Does MarsDawn upload my documents?

No. The app never uploads your documents, collects no data about you and has no account; your documents and settings stay on your Mac. If a document refers to the web and you load that content, your Mac fetches it from the servers that host it, and MarsDawn's developer receives none of it.

More: [Privacy Policy](/privacy/#what-stays-on-your-mac)

### With MCP or the skill, who can see my files?

MarsDawn itself sends nothing. The skill is a text file of instructions, and the marsdawn CLI and the MCP server run on your Mac; the MCP server works only in folders you allow. The one reading your files is your agent, and what it and its model provider do with them is that agent's policy, which MarsDawn neither controls nor describes.

More: [MCP](/cli/mcp/)

### Is it safe to open HTML someone sent me?

By default it opens static: its code doesn't run and nothing loads from the web. If you choose View › Run This Document, that document runs, and it can send data over the network and read images, stylesheets, fonts and media in its folder. The choice is never remembered, so it opens static again next time.

More: [Privacy Policy](/privacy/#when-marsdawn-uses-the-internet)

### Is the site's analytics cookie related to the app?

No. The app and this website are separate: the app collects nothing, and a visit can be recorded only on marsdawn.southern-light.dev. The site's Google Analytics starts denied and sets cookies only after you choose Accept; Cookie settings in the footer changes that. The app's requests for theme files under /themes/ are skipped.

More: [Privacy Policy](/privacy/#the-website)

## Features

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/features/

# Everything MarsDawn does, on one page.

MarsDawn is a Markdown editor for the Mac. You write on one side and read the rendered page on the other, with diagrams, math and code drawn in. It has no AI model of its own: it is built for reading what an agent wrote, and for writing your own. And when the work moves to a table, a meeting or a filing cabinet, it prints and exports clean pages.

Each section below says what the app does and links to the page that goes deeper.

![MarsDawn in split view: the Markdown source on the left, the rendered page on the right.](https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/assets/screens/01-split-1180.png)

In this screenshot:

1. A native Mac window.
2. The Mac's text editor, with Markdown highlighting.
3. ⌘1 source, ⌘2 split, ⌘3 preview.
4. The page updates as you type.

## Read what your agent wrote

### Source and preview, side by side

Open a Markdown file and read the rendered page next to its source (⌘2), or switch to source only (⌘1) or preview only (⌘3). The two panes scroll together, and the page updates as you type.

[A Mac app](/native/)

### Outline and Files sidebar

The sidebar's Outline tab lists a document's headings; click one to jump there. Open a folder and the Files tab lists what is in it, and new files appear on their own while an agent is writing into it. If the folder is a git checkout, the header names the branch or worktree.

[Reading what your agent hands back](/reading-agent-output/)

### Point at the exact line

Edit ▸ Copy Reference copies your place as a path and line, like `docs/plan.md:42`. Copy for AI adds the selected text under it. Paste either into the agent's chat.

[Reading what your agent hands back](/reading-agent-output/)

### Follow links between files

Click a link to another Markdown file in the preview and MarsDawn opens it, or brings it forward if it is already open, and scrolls to the heading.

## On paper, among people

Not all of the work happens on a screen. The pages MarsDawn prints and exports are the ones you read on screen, so they work where people meet, read and keep records.

### In the meeting

Print the pages, or send everyone the same PDF, and the whole table works from the same document instead of one shared screen. Everyone holding the same file has the same page breaks, so "the table on page 3" points at one thing. Then the people write the decisions down, on the printout or in notes. The meeting-notes template starts with decisions and gives each action item an owner.

[PDF export](/pdf/) · [Meeting notes template](/templates/meeting-notes/)

### Reading with a pen

Some people take things in better with a pen: underlining, writing in the margin, so it sticks. Print the document and do that on paper. MarsDawn has no annotation tool of its own, so if you would rather mark up the PDF, use the PDF app you already have.

[PDF export](/pdf/)

### Paper records

Some fields still file paper, accounting among them. MarsDawn makes no archival or compliance claim. What it does is print and export clean, paginated pages: diagrams drawn in, short code blocks kept whole, the theme's light colors. Use them wherever paper is still the record.

[PDF export](/pdf/)

### Handing it to someone who doesn't use Markdown

A PDF opens in anything and needs no Markdown knowledge, so it is also the one to send a manager or a client.

[Sharing exported PDFs](/sharing-exported-pdfs/)

## Write and lay out

### Plain Markdown, highlighted

Bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links, block quotes and task lists all work. The editor colors Markdown syntax, and the colors match your preview theme.

[A Mac app](/native/)

### Zoom, line numbers and a status bar

Zoom the source and preview together from 50% to 300%. A line-number gutter runs beside the source, and the status bar shows your line and column, plus word and character counts and reading time for the document or your selection.

### Images

Save the document, then drop or paste an image into the editor. MarsDawn copies it into an assets folder next to the document and writes the link. Images from the web stay hidden until you click Load Images, so opening a document never tells a server you read it.

[Your writing stays on your Mac](/yours/)

### Front matter stays out of the way

A front matter block at the top of a file shows as a collapsed Document info section in the preview and Quick Look, and is left out of the PDF.

### Eight languages

The app is in English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German, French, Spanish and Korean.

[A Mac app](/native/)

## Diagrams, code and math

### Mermaid diagrams

A fenced code block marked `mermaid` is drawn as a diagram. If the diagram has a mistake, the preview shows its source with the error underneath, and clicking the message jumps to that line.

[Mermaid preview on Mac](/mermaid-preview-mac/)

### Highlighted code

Code blocks are highlighted for most common languages. Name the language after the opening fence.

### Math

Math written in KaTeX syntax is drawn in the preview and in Quick Look, and comes through in the exported PDF.

[Why AI output still needs a human reader](/reviewing-ai-output/)

## Themes, PDF and print

### Four themes, light and dark

Dawn, Classic, Modern and Vivid each come in a light and a dark version, and MarsDawn follows your Mac's appearance unless you pick one in Settings. Choose from View ▸ Preview Theme or the palette button in the toolbar.

[Preview themes and PDF export](/themes/)

### More themes

Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Get More Themes… opens a gallery of extra preview themes. Install one and it shows up under View ▸ Preview Theme; Remove takes it away again. The gallery only goes online while it is open.

[Theme gallery](/themes/gallery/) · [Build a theme](/themes/new/)

### Export as PDF, or print

File ▸ Export as PDF… saves a paginated PDF, and File ▸ Print… prints the same pages. Mermaid diagrams are drawn in, code keeps its highlighting, and page breaks avoid splitting a heading from its section or cutting a short code block or diagram in half. The PDF always uses the theme's light colors, even if you were reading in dark.

[PDF export](/pdf/)

![A PDF exported from MarsDawn, open in its PDF viewer with page thumbnails.](https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/assets/screens/05-pdf-980.png)

In this screenshot:

1. Mermaid diagrams, drawn into the PDF.
2. Code keeps its highlighting.

## Files, tabs and Quick Look

### Windows and tabs

Each document opens in its own window. Choose Window ▸ Merge All Windows to gather open windows as tabs of one. Autosave runs as you type.

[A Mac app](/native/)

### Quick Look in Finder

Select a Markdown file in Finder and press Space to read it rendered, diagrams included. Quick Look uses the theme you picked in MarsDawn and follows its Appearance setting.

[A Mac app](/native/) · [Quick Look for Markdown](/quicklook/)

### Other files

MarsDawn also opens plain text files (`.txt`, `.log`, source code) and PDFs. UTF-8 text opens ready to edit, as source only. PDFs open in a viewer with page thumbnails, zoom and search.

### Your files stay yours

There is no account, no sync and no cloud. Documents stay where you save them, and MarsDawn collects no data about you.

[Your writing stays on your Mac](/yours/)

## For agents and scripts

### A free command-line tool

The free `marsdawn` tool is installed separately with Homebrew. `marsdawn export` turns a Markdown file into a PDF, rendered like MarsDawn's preview; it does not need the app. Choose a theme with `--theme` and paper size A4 or Letter. `marsdawn open` opens files in the app for you to review, optionally at a line, and does need the app installed.

[Command Line](/cli/)

### Output a script can read

Add `--json` and both commands return a result an agent or script can parse.

[marsdawn for agents](/cli/agents/)

### Skill and MCP server

An agent skill file teaches a coding agent to open what it wrote in MarsDawn for your review. For clients without a shell, a separate MCP server runs the same export.

[Agent skill](/cli/skill/) · [MCP server](/cli/mcp/)

### No AI inside

MarsDawn has no AI model of its own. It won't summarize or grade what an agent wrote; it keeps a long, changing file readable so you can do the reading.

[What MarsDawn doesn't do](/limits/)

## Siri and Shortcuts

Search for MarsDawn in the Shortcuts app to find three actions: New Markdown Document (from a template), Add Note to Inbox and Open Recent Document. Notes go to `Inbox.md` in the folder you choose in MarsDawn ▸ Settings… ▸ Notes Folder.

[A Mac app](/native/)

## Your writing stays on your Mac

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/yours/

# Your writing stays on your Mac.

MarsDawn has no account, no sync and no cloud. It opens a file, you write, and it saves the file where you chose.

![MarsDawn showing a document in the Classic theme, with the preview filling the window.](https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/assets/screens/02-classic-1180.png)

In this screenshot:

1. A file on your Mac, saved where you choose.
2. The whole toolbar is themes and layouts; there is nothing to sign in to.

## What that means

- There is no account to sign up for or sign in to.
- Nothing syncs to a cloud. Your documents stay where you save them.
- Nothing is tracked. MarsDawn does not collect any data about you, and its App Store privacy label is "Data Not Collected".
- Web images stay blocked until you choose to load them, so opening a document never tells a server you read it. When you do load them, they load over https only.
- Local images show in the preview once you grant access to their folder.

The details are in the [privacy policy](/privacy/).

## Try free, pay once

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/pay-once/

# Try all of it. Then pay once.

MarsDawn is a free download. Start the 14-day trial and every feature works; to keep using it after that, one purchase of USD 4.99 unlocks it. There is no subscription and no account.

![MarsDawn in the Vivid theme, with Markdown source on the left and the rendered page on the right.](https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/assets/screens/04-vivid-1180.png)

In this screenshot:

1. Markdown highlighting in the editor, included.
2. Every theme and every layout is included.
3. Mermaid diagrams, included.
4. Code highlighting, included.

## How it works

1. **Download it free.** MarsDawn is free to download from the Mac App Store.
2. **Try all of it for 14 days.** Start the trial and everything in MarsDawn works for 14 days: every theme and layout, PDF export and printing, and the Siri and Shortcuts actions. Quick Look in Finder works with or without the trial.
3. **Unlock it once.** To keep using it after that, unlock it once for USD 4.99. It's an in-app purchase, not a subscription, so nothing renews and nothing charges you later.

- The trial doesn't charge you either. When it ends, nothing is bought unless you choose to unlock.
- There is no account. MarsDawn never asks you to create one.

## What works when

|  | Trial (days 1–14) | Trial ended, not unlocked | Unlocked |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open a document in MarsDawn | Yes | Opens, with the content covered | Yes |
| Read and edit in MarsDawn (source, preview, Mermaid, math) | Yes | No | Yes |
| Export as PDF and print from MarsDawn | Yes | No | Yes |
| Keep typed text with File ▸ Save As… | Yes | Yes, in a window open when the trial ended | Yes |
| Siri and Shortcuts actions | Yes | No | Yes |
| Quick Look in Finder, with Mermaid diagrams and math | Yes | Yes, unchanged | Yes |
| `marsdawn export` (free command-line tool): PDF with diagrams and math | Yes | Yes, unchanged | Yes |
| Your files on disk | As you saved them | As you saved them; the lock never changes them | As you saved them |

Before you start the trial, MarsDawn shows the trial offer. Starting it costs nothing.

PDF files you open in MarsDawn are locked the same way once the trial ends.

## If you don't unlock

- After 14 days, until you unlock it, you can't read, edit, export or print documents in MarsDawn. A document still opens, but its content is covered.
- Your files don't change. They're ordinary files on your Mac, and Quick Look in Finder keeps showing them.
- The free [`marsdawn` command-line tool](/cli/) keeps exporting them to PDF, trial or not.
- If a document is open in MarsDawn when the trial ends, the text you typed isn't lost: use File ▸ Save As… to keep it.

## Questions and answers

### How much does MarsDawn cost?

MarsDawn is a free download from the Mac App Store. You can use every feature for 14 days, and after that a one-time in-app purchase of USD 4.99 unlocks it.

### Is there a subscription?

No. The unlock is a single purchase, so nothing renews and nothing charges you later. Starting the trial costs nothing either.

### What happens when the 14-day trial ends?

Until you unlock MarsDawn, you can't read, edit, export or print documents in it: they open with their content covered. Your files stay exactly as you saved them.

### Does Quick Look still work after the trial?

Yes. Quick Look in Finder works with or without the trial. The free marsdawn command-line tool also keeps exporting Markdown to PDF.

### Do I need an account?

No. MarsDawn never asks you to create an account.

## A Mac app

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/native/

# Built out of the Mac's own parts.

MarsDawn is a native Mac app for reading and reviewing Markdown, with live split preview, Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math, Quick Look and PDF export, free to try for 14 days and USD 4.99 once to unlock.

The windows, tabs, menus and text editor are the Mac's own. The rendered page is drawn by WebKit, the engine behind Safari.

![MarsDawn in split view: the Markdown source on the left, the rendered page on the right.](https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/assets/screens/01-split-1180.png)

In this screenshot:

1. A native Mac window.
2. The Mac's text editor, with Markdown highlighting.
3. ⌘1 source, ⌘2 split, ⌘3 preview.
4. The page updates as you type.

## What that means

### Editing

- Source, split and preview layouts, one keystroke apart (`⌘1`, `⌘2`, `⌘3`).
- The two panes scroll together, so the paragraph you are editing stays in view.
- Markdown syntax highlighting in the editor, matched to your preview theme.

### The rest of the Mac

- Native windows, tabs, autosave and version history.
- Quick Look: press Space on a Markdown file in Finder for a preview, diagrams included. [How Quick Look works](/quicklook/)
- Siri and Shortcuts: start a new document from a template, add a line to your notes inbox, or reopen a recent document.
- English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German, French, Spanish and Korean.

## What MarsDawn doesn't do

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/limits/

# What MarsDawn doesn't do.

Some things are left out on purpose. If you need one of them, it's better to know now than after you buy.

![MarsDawn in dark mode, with Markdown source on the left and the rendered page on the right.](https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/assets/screens/03-dark-1180.png)

In this screenshot:

1. One document per window, on this Mac.
2. You write Markdown here.
3. The toolbar holds themes and layouts, and there is no plugins menu.
4. The page is for reading, not editing.

## Left out

### Devices and people

- **Sync:** MarsDawn doesn't sync your documents. They stay where you save them, so to use one on another Mac, keep it in a folder you already sync.
- **iPhone and iPad:** there is no app for them; MarsDawn is for the Mac.
- **Sharing:** there are no accounts and no shared editing, because MarsDawn is for one person on their own Mac.
- **System:** MarsDawn needs macOS 26 or later.

### Files and features

- **Editing:** you write Markdown on the left and read the page on the right; the page itself can't be edited.
- **Formats:** MarsDawn exports PDF and prints, and doesn't export Word files.
- **Other files:** plain text files and PDFs open read-only.
- **Themes:** it comes with Dawn, Classic, Modern and Vivid, each in light and dark. More are in the [theme gallery](/themes/gallery/): install one from Settings › Appearance › Get More Themes…, or [build your own](/themes/new/) in the browser. A theme is colours and style settings, not a plugin.
- **Plugins:** MarsDawn has no plugins or extensions.

## After the trial

If you don't unlock MarsDawn once the 14-day trial ends, you can't read, edit, export or print documents in it: they open with their content covered. Your files stay as they are, Quick Look still shows them, and the free command-line tool still exports them. The [trial and unlock page](/pay-once/) sets all three stages side by side.

# Support

Help with MarsDawn, the Markdown editor for macOS.

## Write to us

[support@southern-light.dev](mailto:support@southern-light.dev?subject=MarsDawn%20support)

Invitations to interview or to speak are welcome too. Write to [support@southern-light.dev](mailto:support@southern-light.dev?subject=Interview%20or%20talk%20invitation).

Please include your macOS version and your MarsDawn version (MarsDawn › About MarsDawn). If something looks wrong, a screenshot or a small sample document helps a lot.

## Common questions

### What do I need to run MarsDawn?

A Mac with macOS 26 Tahoe or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

### How do I switch between the editor and the preview?

Press `⌘1` for the source only, `⌘2` for side by side, and `⌘3` for the preview only. The same choices are in the View menu and the toolbar.

### An image in my document doesn't show.

- **Image on your Mac:** save the document first, then click *Grant Folder Access…* in the preview and choose the folder that holds the image. MarsDawn remembers the folder. You can review granted folders in MarsDawn › Settings › Folder Access.
- **Image from the web:** web images are blocked until you click *Load Images* at the top of the preview. To always load them, turn on *Load remote images automatically* in Settings.

### How do I add an image?

Drag it into the editor, or paste it. The document must be saved first: MarsDawn copies the image into an `assets` folder next to the document and writes the Markdown link for you.

### A Mermaid diagram shows an error.

MarsDawn shows the diagram's source with the first line of Mermaid's error message underneath. Check the line it names, for example for an arrow with nothing after it or a bracket that isn't closed.

### How do I make a PDF?

Choose File › Export as PDF… (`⌥⌘E`). The PDF uses the light version of your preview theme and is split into pages, whichever layout you are in. File › Print… prints the same pages.

### How do I use MarsDawn with Siri or Shortcuts?

Open the Shortcuts app and search for MarsDawn to find *New Markdown Document*, *Add Note to Inbox* and *Open Recent Document*. Before adding notes, choose a notes folder in MarsDawn › Settings › Notes Folder. Notes are added to `Inbox.md` in that folder.

### Where are my settings?

MarsDawn › Settings (`⌘,`) has appearance, images, the notes folder, folder access and the preview theme.

### How do I get a refund?

Purchases are handled by Apple. Request a refund at [reportaproblem.apple.com](https://reportaproblem.apple.com).

## Privacy Policy

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/privacy/

# Privacy Policy

How MarsDawn, the Markdown editor for macOS, handles your information.

Last updated 2026-10-12

> **The MarsDawn app does not collect any data about you.** There is no account, no advertising and no tracking. Your documents and settings stay on your Mac.

## The website

The app and this website are two different things. The app collects nothing. A visit can be recorded only here, on marsdawn.southern-light.dev.

This site uses **Google Analytics 4**, loaded through **Google Tag Manager**. Every visitor starts with analytics denied: Google's Consent Mode sends only a cookieless ping with no analytics cookie and no persistent identifier, until you choose *Accept* in the banner. Choosing *Decline*, or making no choice at all, keeps it that way, and choosing *Decline* after a prior *Accept* turns analytics back off immediately and removes the cookies below. Change your choice at any time with the "Cookie settings" link in the footer of every page. The choice itself is stored only in your browser's local storage, never in a cookie of ours.

Once you accept, Google Analytics sets its own cookies (`_ga` and `_ga_<measurement id>`) and records:

- **Page views and referrer.** Which page was viewed, and the referring address when the browser sends one.
- **Approximate location, device and browser.** A coarse location derived from your IP address (city level at most), your device type, operating system and browser — none of it precise enough to identify you.
- **Outbound clicks and scroll depth.** Google Analytics' enhanced measurement records clicks that leave the site, such as the link to the Mac App Store, and how far you scroll down a page.
- **IP addresses.** Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses.
- **What is not recorded.** No account, because the site has none. No document, and nothing you type. No cross-site advertising, and no profile of you. Requests the app makes for theme files under `/themes/` are skipped, and are not sent on. The theme simulator and gallery on `/themes/new/` and `/themes/gallery/` run entirely in your browser and send no theme data to Google Analytics either.
- **Retention.** Google keeps this data for 14 months, then deletes it.
- **Where it's processed.** Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics are operated by Google; your data may be processed in the United States as well as other countries where Google operates.
- **The host.** Cloudflare hosts the site and, like any host, sees your IP address while it answers the request. That log belongs to the host. It is not the analytics above.

## Launch survey

From 20 October to 2 November 2026, MarsDawn runs a short survey on Google Forms. Filling it in is up to you, and the app itself still collects nothing.

- **What it collects.** Your answers and the email address you type. Nothing else.
- **The email.** It's used to send you a code if you're drawn. If you don't tick the update box, it's deleted within 30 days after the codes are sent. If you tick it, it's kept only to send MarsDawn version-update emails, each with a one-click unsubscribe, until you unsubscribe.
- **The answers.** After the draw they're kept without the email, and they may appear anonymised and aggregated in a published summary.
- **Never shared or sold,** and never used for anything else.
- **Where it's stored.** Google Forms stores the responses with Google, under Google's privacy policy.
- **Deletion.** To have your response or email deleted sooner, write to support@southern-light.dev.

## What stays on your Mac

- **Your documents.** MarsDawn reads and writes only the files and folders you open, save or choose. They are never uploaded anywhere by the app.
- **Your settings.** Appearance, preview theme, window layout and the image preference are stored in the app's own preferences on your Mac.
- **Folder access you grant.** When you let MarsDawn show images or page files from a folder, or choose a notes folder, the app keeps a macOS bookmark so it can open that folder again. A folder you open in the sidebar stays readable and writable by MarsDawn until you remove it in Settings, not just while its window is open. You can remove folders at any time in MarsDawn › Settings.

## When MarsDawn uses the internet

MarsDawn works fully offline. It connects to the internet only **when you choose to**: for a document that refers to the web, or for the theme gallery. For documents:

- **Markdown documents.** Web images are blocked by default. They load only after you click *Load Images* in the preview, or if you turn on *Load remote images automatically* in Settings. Nothing else a Markdown document refers to is loaded from the web.
- **HTML documents.** An HTML document opens static: its code doesn't run and nothing is loaded from the web. If a document contains code that could run, you can choose *View › Run This Document* for that document. Its own code then runs until you stop it, the document reloads or you close the window. That choice is never remembered, and it isn't a setting. While it runs, the document can send data over the network, and read images, style sheets, fonts and media in its folder and the folders inside it. Code downloaded from the web never runs.

MarsDawn loads web content over https only. A plain http address is never loaded, in any setting, and MarsDawn does not rewrite it to https. In a Markdown document, the preview shows a placeholder in its place.

When web content loads, your Mac requests it directly from the servers that host it. Like any web request, this lets those servers see your IP address and what was requested. MarsDawn's developer receives none of this information.

Links you click in the preview open in your default web browser, under that browser's own privacy practices. Audio and video never play by themselves.

If you open *Settings › Appearance › Get More Themes…*, choose *Check for Theme Updates*, or install or update a theme, MarsDawn downloads the theme list, previews and theme files from marsdawn.southern-light.dev. Themes update automatically only during these downloads, never in the background. The request carries no account, identifier, cookie or document data; like any web request, our host Cloudflare sees your IP address and which files were requested. *Report Theme…* makes no request from the app: it only opens a GitHub or email link in your browser or mail app.

## Siri, Shortcuts and Spotlight

MarsDawn offers actions for Siri, the Shortcuts app and Spotlight, such as creating a document or adding a note. When you use them, the text you provide is passed to MarsDawn on your Mac and saved only where the action says (a new document, or the `Inbox.md` file in the notes folder you chose). Speech you dictate to Siri is handled by Apple under [Apple's Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).

## Exporting and printing

PDF export and printing happen on your Mac. The PDF is saved where you choose. Printing goes through macOS to the printer you pick.

## The marsdawn command-line tool

The optional `marsdawn` command-line tool, distributed separately, also runs entirely on your Mac. It reads the Markdown file you name and writes the PDF you ask for. It loads web images only when you pass `--allow-remote-images`.

## Children

The MarsDawn app does not collect data from anyone, including children. A visit recorded on the website is not an account, and it is not used to identify anyone.

## Purchases

MarsDawn is sold through the Mac App Store. Apple processes the purchase under its own terms, and the developer never receives your payment details.

## Changes to this policy

If MarsDawn ever starts handling data differently, this page will be updated before that version is released, and the date at the top will change.

## Contact

Questions about privacy: [support@southern-light.dev](mailto:support@southern-light.dev)

## How to open .md files on Mac

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/view-markdown-on-mac/

# How to open .md files on Mac.

Double-click it. If your Mac opens it in a text editor and you see `#` and `**` instead of headings and bold, the file is fine: a `.md` file is plain text, and that editor is showing the text as it is. Open it in an app that renders Markdown, such as MarsDawn, and make that app the default so every `.md` file opens there.

A `.md` file is plain text. The headings, bold words, tables and diagrams are written as marks: `#` for a heading, `**` around bold, pipes for a table, a `mermaid` code block for a diagram. Open it in a plain text editor and you read the marks. To read the page the way its author meant, something has to render it.

## Open a .md file on your Mac

1. **Double-click the file.** It opens in the app your Mac has set for `.md` files. With no Markdown app, that is often a plain text editor, which shows the marks instead of the page.
2. **Pick the app yourself.** Control-click the file and choose Open With, then the app. Or choose File ▸ Get Info (⌘I), pick an app under "Open with:", and click "Change All…" so every file of this type opens there. MarsDawn opens `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd` and `.mkdn` files.
3. **Preview without opening it.** Select the file in Finder and press Space. With MarsDawn installed, Quick Look shows the rendered page, diagrams included.

## Read it in MarsDawn

MarsDawn is a Markdown editor for the Mac. It is free to download from the Mac App Store: try everything for 14 days, then unlock it once for USD 4.99. No subscription, no account. It needs macOS 26 or later.

[Download MarsDawn free on the Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812925073)

Open a `.md` file and read the rendered page next to the source:

- The preview updates as you type, and the two panes scroll together.
- [Mermaid](/mermaid-preview-mac/) flowcharts and sequence diagrams are drawn in the preview, and code blocks are highlighted.
- When you want to change something, the source is right there. MarsDawn is an editor, not only a viewer.

If an AI agent wrote the file, this is the loop MarsDawn is built for: the agent writes, you read it rendered, and it revises. See [the home page](/), and [marsdawn for agents](/cli/agents/) for letting an agent open files for you. For why that reading matters and how to review a plan, see [Reading what your agent hands back](/reading-agent-output/) and [Reviewing an agent plan in five minutes](/reviewing-agent-plans/).

## Without the app: turn it into a PDF

The free `marsdawn` command-line tool renders a Markdown file to a PDF, which any Mac can open. Tables, math, Mermaid diagrams and highlighted code come out rendered, and it needs nothing else installed, not even the MarsDawn app.

```
brew tap redtear1115/tap && brew install marsdawn
marsdawn export notes.md
open notes.pdf
```

`export` writes `notes.pdf` next to the Markdown file, and `open` shows it in your PDF viewer. It needs macOS 15 or later. The walk-through, with a real exported page, is on [Markdown to PDF](/markdown-to-pdf/).

## Questions

### What is a .md file?

A `.md` file is a plain text file written in Markdown, a way of marking up text with simple characters: `#` for a heading, `**` around bold, a pipe for a table cell. The extensions `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd` and `.mkdn` mean the same thing. Developers use it for READMEs and docs, and AI agents often hand back their plans and reports as `.md` files.

### Why does my .md file open as plain text, with # and ** marks in it?

Because it is plain text, and a plain text editor shows it as it is. Nothing is wrong with the file. To see headings, bold, tables and diagrams, open it in an app that renders Markdown. In MarsDawn the rendered page sits next to the source.

### Why does it open with garbled characters?

Garbled characters usually mean the file was saved in a text encoding other than UTF-8, and the app that opened it guessed wrong. The fix is to save a UTF-8 copy. MarsDawn opens a plain text file that isn't UTF-8 read-only, names the encoding it read it as in a bar at the top of the window, and offers Save As UTF-8… there, or File ▸ Save As… (⌥⇧⌘S), to write a UTF-8 copy you can edit.

### Can I turn a .md file into a PDF?

Yes. In MarsDawn, choose File ▸ Export as PDF… (⌥⌘E) or File ▸ Print…; the pages are paginated, with diagrams drawn in and code highlighted, in the theme's light colors. Without the app, the free `marsdawn export` command-line tool makes the same PDF: `marsdawn export notes.md`. See [PDF export](/pdf/) and [Markdown to PDF](/markdown-to-pdf/).

### Can I open the .md files my AI agent wrote?

Yes, that is what MarsDawn is built for. Open the file and read the rendered page next to its source; when the agent revises it, open it again. An agent can also run `marsdawn open plan.md` to open the file in MarsDawn for you. See [Reading what your agent hands back](/reading-agent-output/).

## Mermaid preview on Mac

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/mermaid-preview-mac/

# Mermaid preview on Mac.

Mermaid lets you write a diagram as text inside a Markdown file. Most editors show you the text. MarsDawn draws the diagram: in the preview next to the source, in Quick Look in Finder, and in the PDF you export.

## Write the diagram as text

Put the diagram in a code block marked `mermaid`:

````
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Write[Write Markdown] --> Preview[Live preview]
    Preview --> Export{Share it?}
    Export -- PDF --> PDF[File ▸ Export as PDF…]
    Export -- Print --> Print[File ▸ Print…]
```
````

In MarsDawn that block becomes a flowchart: Write Markdown, then Live preview, then a Share it? choice that leads to PDF or Print.

![The Dawn theme in split view: Markdown source on the left, the rendered page on the right.](/assets/screens/01-split-800.png)

## Where the diagram is drawn

- **In the preview.** Open the file and the diagram sits next to its source (⌘2). The page updates as you type, and the two panes scroll together.
- **In Quick Look.** Select the file in Finder and press Space; diagrams are drawn there too.
- **In the PDF.** File ▸ Export as PDF… and File ▸ Print… draw the diagram into the page. Page breaks avoid cutting a diagram in half. The PDF uses the theme's light colors.
- **From the command line.** The free `marsdawn export` tool draws the same diagrams into a PDF, and does not need the app. See [Command Line](/cli/).
- **In your theme.** The preview's Appearance setting applies to diagrams too, so a diagram follows light or dark.

## When the diagram has a mistake

If Mermaid can't draw a diagram, the preview shows the diagram's source with the full error message underneath. When the error names a line, click the message and the editor jumps to that line. `marsdawn export --json` reports failed diagrams in `diagramErrors`, so a script or an agent can tell that a diagram didn't draw.

## What to know

- You edit the Mermaid text. There is no visual diagram editor, and you can't drag boxes in the preview.
- Which diagram types draw depends on the Mermaid version inside the app. MarsDawn 1.1.0 includes Mermaid 12.0.0. The kit's export tests render documents for flowcharts, sequence, class, state, entity-relationship, Gantt, pie, mindmap, journey, timeline and git graphs, among others.
- MarsDawn has no AI model, so it doesn't write a diagram for you. The [flowchart template](/templates/flowchart/) has a prompt you can hand to your own agent.

## Quick Look for Markdown

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/quicklook/

# Preview Markdown in Finder with Quick Look.

Select a Markdown file in Finder and press Space. With MarsDawn installed, Quick Look shows the rendered page instead of plain text.

## What the preview shows

- The rendered page, drawn by the same renderer as MarsDawn's preview pane.
- Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math and highlighted code blocks.
- The preview theme you picked in MarsDawn, in light or dark.
- Web images stay blocked, and pictures stored next to the file can appear as placeholders.

## How to preview a Markdown file with Quick Look

1. **Install MarsDawn.** Download MarsDawn from the Mac App Store. The Quick Look extension is part of the app.
2. **Select a Markdown file.** In Finder, click a .md file once.
3. **Press Space.** The rendered preview opens. Press Space again to close it.
4. **If you see plain text, switch the extension on.** Open System Settings, go to General ▸ Login Items & Extensions, click the Info button next to Quick Look under Extensions, turn on MarsDawn Preview, then click Done.

## Not locked by the trial

Quick Look keeps working after the trial ends. It shows the same rendered preview while the trial runs, after it ends and after you unlock. After the trial ends and until you unlock, MarsDawn's own windows open with their content covered; Finder previews are unchanged. The [trial and unlock page](/pay-once/) sets all three stages side by side.

## Questions and answers

### How do I preview a Markdown file in Finder?

Select the file and press Space. With MarsDawn installed, Quick Look shows the rendered page, with Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math and highlighted code.

### Does Quick Look still work after the 14-day trial?

Yes. Quick Look is not locked by the trial. It keeps rendering Markdown files while the trial runs, after it ends and once you unlock.

### Why does Quick Look show plain text?

The Quick Look extension may be switched off. Open System Settings, go to General ▸ Login Items & Extensions, click the Info button next to Quick Look under Extensions, turn on MarsDawn Preview, then click Done.

### Does Quick Look cost extra?

No. The Quick Look extension is part of MarsDawn, with no separate purchase. MarsDawn is a free download with a 14-day trial and a one-time USD 4.99 unlock, and Quick Look works with or without the trial.

### Which version of macOS does it need?

MarsDawn needs macOS 26 or later.

## Markdown to PDF

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/markdown-to-pdf/

# Markdown to PDF on a Mac, from the command line.

The free `marsdawn` tool turns a Markdown file into a PDF with one command. Tables, math, Mermaid diagrams and highlighted code come out the way they read in the source, and it needs nothing else installed, not even the MarsDawn app.

## Install it

```
brew install redtear1115/tap/marsdawn
marsdawn --version
```

On an Apple silicon Mac, Homebrew installs a prebuilt copy in seconds. On an Intel Mac it builds from source instead, which takes a few minutes and needs Xcode 26 or later. It runs on macOS 15 or later, and `marsdawn --version` prints the version you got.

## Save a document

Paste this into a file named `plan.md`:

````
# Plan: faster exports

An agent wrote this plan. You review it, then turn it into a PDF.

## Steps

| Step | Owner | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| Measure the slow pages | Agent | Done |
| Cache rendered diagrams | Agent | In review |

The target is $t < 2\,\text{s}$ for a 50-page document:

$$
t_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} t_i
$$

```mermaid
graph LR
  Draft --> Review --> Ship
```

```swift
let pdf = try export("plan.md")
```
````

## Export it

```
marsdawn export plan.md
```

It writes `plan.pdf` next to the source and prints where it went:

```
Exported /Users/you/plan.pdf (1 page)
```

This is that page, captured from a real run of `marsdawn` 0.5.0:

![The exported PDF: the heading, a table of steps, an inline and a displayed formula, a Draft, Review, Ship diagram, and a highlighted line of Swift.](/assets/cli/plan-en.png)

## Choose a theme, paper size and file name

```
marsdawn export plan.md --theme classic --paper letter -o handout.pdf
```

- `--theme`: dawn, classic, modern or vivid, in the theme's light colors. Without it, `export` uses `$MARSDAWN_THEME`, then dawn.
- `--paper`: a4 or letter. The default is a4.
- `-o`: where to write the PDF, instead of next to the source.
- `--allow-remote-images`: load images from the web while rendering. They stay off unless you pass it.

## If it doesn't work

- `A full installation of Xcode.app 26.0 is required to compile this software.` Homebrew is building `marsdawn` from source, as it does on an Intel Mac. Install Xcode 26 or later from the App Store, then run the install again.
- `marsdawn: No such file: …` The path doesn't point at a file. Check the name, or run the command from the folder the file is in.
- `… already exists. Pass --force to replace it.` A PDF with that name is already there. Add `--force` to replace it, or `-o` to write it somewhere else.
- `Error: The value '…' is invalid for '--theme <theme>'.` The theme or paper size isn't one it knows. The themes are dawn, classic, modern and vivid; the paper is a4 or letter.

- kit · [https://github.com/redtear1115/mars-dawn-kit/blob/0.6.4/README.md?plain=1#L7](https://github.com/redtear1115/mars-dawn-kit/blob/0.6.4/README.md?plain=1#L7)

What MarsDawn lacks. It needs macOS 26 or later. There is no iPhone or iPad app; MarsDawn is for the Mac. There's no shared editing, no sync and no account. The preview can't be edited; you edit the Markdown source beside it. It doesn't export Word files and has no plugins. Its PDFs have no page numbers. There's no diff view: when an agent saves a change, the open window updates from disk in one step you can undo, but it doesn't highlight what changed. After the 14-day trial, documents open with their content covered until you unlock it.

## When you don't need MarsDawn

- You live in VS Code and a preview pane is enough: it renders Mermaid and KaTeX, shows Markdown diff previews and jumps to a line with code -g.
- You only want a space-bar preview in Finder: QLMarkdown is a free Quick Look extension for Markdown.
- Your Mac runs an older macOS: QLMarkdown needs 12.0 or later and LynxOffice 13 or later. The free marsdawn tool needs macOS 15 and exports PDF without the app.
- You keep a vault of linked notes: that is what Obsidian is built for.
- You need an iPhone or iPad app, shared editing or Word export.
- You want an agent to handle spreadsheets, Word files and PDFs: LynxOffice documents an MCP server for them.

- [MacMD Viewer vs. MarsDawn](/vs/macmd-viewer/): a read-only viewer next to MarsDawn, cell by cell, with when to pick each.
- [Markdown preview tools](/vs/markdown-preview-tools/): VS Code's preview, a browser extension and Claude Desktop's file preview.
- [Best Markdown viewer for Mac (2026)](/best-markdown-viewer-mac/)

## MacMD Viewer vs. MarsDawn

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/vs/macmd-viewer/

# MacMD Viewer vs. MarsDawn.

Both are Mac apps for reading Markdown as a finished page. MacMD Viewer opens a `.md` file and shows it; it is read-only by design and never saves changes to your file. MarsDawn puts an editor next to the same kind of rendered preview, so you write and review in one window. This page sets the two side by side, row by row, with a source for every fact about MacMD Viewer, and says when MacMD Viewer is the better choice.

Checked against MacMD Viewer's own site and repository on 15 October 2026 (version 1.7.0, released 10 October 2026). If something here is out of date, tell us at the address on the [support page](/support/).

## What it is and what it does

|  | MacMD Viewer | MarsDawn |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | A viewer: "read-only and never saves changes to your source file" [[S1](#s1), [S9](#s9)] | An editor with a live preview: Markdown on the left, the rendered page on the right, in three layouts (source, split, preview) |
| Editing | No [[S1](#s1), [S7](#s7), [S9](#s9)] | Yes. The rendered page itself isn't editable; you edit the source beside it |
| Live preview | Renders the file; reloads when the file is saved by another editor [[S9](#s9)] | Updates as you type. When another app changes the file, MarsDawn reloads it and keeps your place, as long as you have no unsaved edits of your own. |
| Mermaid | Yes: flowcharts, sequence, state and Gantt diagrams, pie charts and more, offline [[S1](#s1), [S3](#s3), [S7](#s7)] | Yes |
| Math | No: its README says it "does not render math (LaTeX/KaTeX)" [[S7](#s7)] | Yes, KaTeX |
| Code highlighting | Yes [[S1](#s1), [S9](#s9)] | Yes |
| Themes | 12 document themes [[S1](#s1), [S7](#s7)] | 4 built in (Dawn, Classic, Modern, Vivid), each with a light and a dark palette, plus more in the theme gallery |
| Tabs | Yes, optional and off by default (since 1.6.0) [[S5](#s5), [S8](#s8)] | Yes |
| PDF export | Yes, one continuous page, in the current theme, no watermark [[S3](#s3), [S9](#s9)] | Yes, paginated pages in the theme's light palette; page breaks avoid splitting short code blocks |
| Print | Yes, through the macOS print dialog [[S3](#s3), [S9](#s9)] | Yes |
| Quick Look in Finder | Yes, included; you enable it in System Settings; uses your theme [[S4](#s4)] | Yes, works with or without the trial; uses your theme |
| Mermaid and math in Quick Look | Mermaid: yes [[S4](#s4)]. Math: no, it doesn't render math [[S7](#s7)] | Yes, both are drawn |
| Command line | No standalone command-line tool is described. It has a `markdownviewer://` URL scheme and a Claude Code plugin and hooks that open files in the viewer [[S6](#s6)] | The free `marsdawn` tool: `marsdawn export` renders a PDF without the app, `marsdawn open` opens a file at a line |
| Interface languages | Not stated in its own materials [[S1](#s1), [S3](#s3), [S7](#s7)] | English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German, French, Spanish and Korean |
| Requires | macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later; Apple Silicon and Intel [[S1](#s1), [S7](#s7)] | macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later |
| Other platforms | Mac only [[S1](#s1)] | Mac only. No iPhone or iPad app |

| Price | USD 19.99 once, for one active Mac (movable to another Mac); Family Pack USD 39.99 for 3; 10 keys USD 129 [[S2](#s2)] | Free download, then USD 4.99 once |

|---|---|---|

## Which one to pick

**Pick MacMD Viewer if** you only read Markdown and you want that to be guaranteed: it never saves changes to your file [[S1](#s1)]. It also fits better if your Mac runs macOS 14 or 15, since MarsDawn needs macOS 26 [[S1](#s1), [S7](#s7)]; if you would rather buy from a developer's own site, Homebrew or Setapp than the Mac App Store [[S2](#s2), [S7](#s7)]; if you want files an agent edits to open in the viewer automatically, which it does through hooks for Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf [[S6](#s6)]; or if you want a single continuous-page PDF rather than paginated pages [[S9](#s9)]. It has no trial, but it has a 14-day refund [[S2](#s2)].

**Pick MarsDawn if** the Markdown comes back for another pass. An agent's plan, README or spec usually needs a fix, a reworded line or a new section, and in MarsDawn you do that in the window where you are already reading. It also covers math (KaTeX), which MacMD Viewer says it doesn't render [[S7](#s7)]; it ships in eight interface languages; it has a free `marsdawn` command line that exports a PDF without the app; and its price is USD 4.99 after a 14-day trial in which everything works.

**Either works if** you read Markdown on a recent Mac, want Mermaid diagrams drawn properly and want Quick Look in Finder. Both do those.

**And you can use both.** They aren't exclusive: nothing stops you from keeping a read-only viewer for what you only read and an editor for what you write.

## Questions

### Does MacMD Viewer edit files?

No. It is read-only and, in its own words, never saves changes to your source file [[S1](#s1), [S9](#s9)]. It can open the file in your text editor (File menu, ⇧⌘E, since 1.7.0), which hands the file to another app [[S5](#s5)].

### Is MacMD Viewer on the Mac App Store?

Its own pages list its site, Homebrew and Setapp, and don't mention the Mac App Store [[S2](#s2), [S7](#s7)]. MarsDawn is on the Mac App Store only.

### Can MarsDawn open the same files?

Yes. It opens `.md` files, and also plain text files and PDFs: text opens ready to edit as UTF-8, and PDFs open in a viewer.

### What if I'm on macOS 14 or 15?

MacMD Viewer runs on macOS 14 or later [[S1](#s1)]. MarsDawn needs macOS 26 or later, and the free `marsdawn` command-line tool can still export a PDF.

### Why is one USD 19.99 and the other USD 4.99?

They differ in what you get and how you pay. MacMD Viewer is a one-time purchase with a 14-day refund and no trial [[S2](#s2)]. MarsDawn is a free download with a 14-day trial, then a one-time unlock. Neither is a subscription.

## Try it today, free

MarsDawn is on the Mac App Store. The free `marsdawn` command-line tool also renders any Markdown file to a PDF, with Mermaid diagrams and highlighted code, and needs nothing else installed:

```
brew tap redtear1115/tap && brew install marsdawn
marsdawn export notes.md
open notes.pdf
```

## Best Markdown viewer for Mac (2026)

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/best-markdown-viewer-mac/

# Best Markdown viewer for Mac (2026)

The best Markdown viewer depends on what you read. If it is notes you write yourself, an all-in-one editor is enough. If it is long documents with diagrams and math, or files an AI agent keeps rewriting, check how each app handles live reload, Mermaid and PDF. The apps below are in alphabetical order, and each one gets who it suits, one honest drawback and its price.

## MacDown 3000

The original MacDown is no longer maintained. MacDown 3000 is the community continuation: free and open source (MIT), native, with Mermaid, MathJax, PDF export, live reload and Quick Look.

- Suits: people who want a free native split view.
- Drawback: no documented way to open a file at a line from the command line.
- Price: free.

## Marked

Marked 3 is a previewer for Markdown you write in another app. It reloads whenever the file changes, has MathJax and KaTeX, and prints paginated PDFs with page numbers. Marked 2 is still sold.

- Suits: writers who keep their own editor and want a polished preview and print.
- Drawback: Quick Look is a separate app, Marked QL (USD 9.99).
- Price: Marked 3 is a free download, then USD 2.99/month, USD 29.99/year or USD 69.99 lifetime. Marked 2 is USD 14.99 direct or USD 13.99 on the Mac App Store.

## MarkEdit

A light, free native editor (CodeMirror in a web view) with Quick Look.

- Suits: people who want a fast plain-text editor that feels at home on the Mac.
- Drawback: Mermaid and math need the official extensions, and PDF export needs Pandoc.
- Price: free.

## MarsDawn

A native Mac app that shows the source and a live preview side by side, with Mermaid and KaTeX built in. When an agent saves the file, the open window takes the change as one undoable "Update from Disk". `marsdawn open notes.md:120` opens a file at a line, and there is a skill and an MCP server for agents. Quick Look works with or without the trial. Copy for AI and Copy Reference hand text to an agent. Nothing leaves your Mac unless you choose.

- Suits: people reviewing Markdown that AI agents write.
- Drawback: the PDF export has no page numbers.
- Price: free download with a 14-day trial, then USD 4.99 once. No account. Mac App Store only.

## Obsidian

A notes app built around a vault of linked Markdown files, with Mermaid, MathJax, PDF export and live reload.

- Suits: people building a knowledge base of their own notes.
- Drawback: it is an Electron app, and it works best with files inside a vault.
- Price: free. Sync and Publish are paid.

## QLMarkdown

A Quick Look extension: select a .md file in Finder and press Space. Mermaid and MathJax are opt-in.

- Suits: people who only want to glance at files in Finder.
- Drawback: it is not an app for reading or editing, and has no documented PDF export.
- Price: free (GPL-3.0).

## Typora

A seamless editor where the preview is the document, with Mermaid, MathJax and PDF export with page numbers in the header or footer.

- Suits: people who prefer to write in a WYSIWYG-style view.
- Drawback: no separate source and preview side by side.
- Price: USD 14.99 once, for up to 3 devices.

## VS Code preview

The built-in Markdown preview, with Mermaid built in since 1.121 and KaTeX. `code -g file:line` opens a file at a line.

- Suits: developers who already live in VS Code.
- Drawback: it is an Electron app, and has no built-in PDF export.
- Price: free.

## Comparison

| App | Price | Mermaid | Math | PDF | Live reload | CLI at line | Quick Look | Build |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MacDown 3000 | Free | Yes | MathJax | Yes | Yes | Not documented | Yes | Native |
| Marked 3 | From USD 2.99/mo | Yes | MathJax, KaTeX | Yes, page numbers | Yes | Not documented | Marked QL, USD 9.99 | Native |
| MarkEdit | Free | Extension | KaTeX (extension) | Pandoc | Not documented | Not documented | Yes | Native (web view) |
| MarsDawn | USD 4.99 once | Yes | KaTeX | Yes, no page numbers | Yes, undoable | Yes | Yes | Native |
| Obsidian | Free | Yes | MathJax | Yes | Yes | Not documented | Not documented | Electron |
| QLMarkdown | Free | Opt-in | MathJax (opt-in) | Not documented | n/a | n/a | It is one | Native |
| Typora | USD 14.99 once | Yes | MathJax | Yes, page numbers | Not documented | Not documented | Not documented | Native |
| VS Code | Free | Yes (1.121+) | KaTeX | No | Not documented | Yes | Not documented | Electron |

## Who MarsDawn is not for

- You need page numbers in your PDFs. Typora and Marked 3 add them, MarsDawn does not.
- You keep a linked knowledge base of your own notes. Obsidian is built for that.
- You never leave VS Code. Its built-in preview is free, and VS Code is adding an experimental Markdown view to its Agents window.
- You only want a preview in Finder. QLMarkdown is free.

## FAQ

### Which free Markdown viewers for Mac have Mermaid?

MacDown 3000, Obsidian and VS Code (1.121 and later) have it built in. QLMarkdown has it as an option, and MarkEdit through an extension.

### Which ones export PDF with page numbers?

Typora and Marked 3. MarsDawn exports PDF without page numbers.

### Which ones open a file at a specific line from the command line?

MarsDawn (`marsdawn open notes.md:120`) and VS Code (`code -g file:line`). For the others it is not documented.

### Which ones are native Mac apps rather than Electron?

All of them except Obsidian and VS Code. MarkEdit is native with its editor in a web view.

[Download and try it free](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812925073)

## Command Line

Source: https://marsdawn.southern-light.dev/cli/

# Command Line

The free `marsdawn` command-line tool: export Markdown to PDF from a shell or an LLM agent, and, with the MarsDawn app installed, open files in it.

**marsdawn is free and distributed separately from the Mac App Store.** Install it with Homebrew: on an Apple silicon Mac it arrives ready to run. `export` works on its own; `open` needs the MarsDawn app.

Calling marsdawn from an AI agent or a script? See [marsdawn for agents](/cli/agents/) for the JSON output, its schemas and every exit code, or [the MCP server](/cli/mcp/) if your agent calls tools over MCP instead.

## Install

With [Homebrew](https://brew.sh):

```
brew tap redtear1115/tap && brew install marsdawn
```

Using a coding agent? Run `marsdawn skill --install` to add [the marsdawn skill](/cli/skill/): one file that teaches it to open what it wrote in MarsDawn for your review, and to export PDFs.

On an Apple silicon Mac, Homebrew installs a prebuilt copy in seconds, with nothing else to install. On an Intel Mac it builds marsdawn from source instead, which takes a few minutes and needs Xcode 26 or later (Swift 6.2). The tool runs on macOS 15 or later.

Or build it from [the source](https://github.com/redtear1115/mars-dawn-kit) with Swift Package Manager:

```
git clone https://github.com/redtear1115/mars-dawn-kit.git
cd mars-dawn-kit
swift build -c release --product marsdawn
```

Check which version you have with `marsdawn --version`.

## Commands

### marsdawn open

Opens one or more Markdown files in the MarsDawn app for review. It needs the app installed: without it, `marsdawn open` exits with code 3 and says MarsDawn isn't installed. `export` doesn't need the app. The app is on the [Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812925073).

```
marsdawn open notes.md
marsdawn open notes.md:120
marsdawn open notes.md --line 120
marsdawn open .
marsdawn open notes.md --folder .
```

- `path:line`: asks MarsDawn to land on that line. A column after it, as in `notes.md:120:8`, is ignored. If a file with the whole name exists, the argument is that file.
- `--line <n>`: the same for a single file, and the way to ask for a line on a path that itself ends in a colon and digits. Needs exactly one file.
- Lines run from 1 to 999999999.
- MarsDawn 1.0 opens the file at that line.
- A folder argument opens in the window's sidebar instead of as a document: `marsdawn open .` shows the current folder. `--folder <path>` does the same alongside files. A window's sidebar shows one folder, so naming two is a usage error.
- `--wait <n>`: with MarsDawn 1.0.2 or later, which reports back, `--folder` waits up to n seconds (0 to 30, default 2) for the app's answer about the folder. `--wait 0`, or an app that doesn't report back, doesn't wait and sends the same request as before.
- A `--wait` value outside 0 to 30 is a usage error (exit 64). Write a negative value as `--wait=-1`.
- With `--json`, the folder is reported as requested, not attached, because the app decides; with `--wait`, the result also says what happened to it. The full list is in [marsdawn for agents](/cli/agents/).
- `--background`: open without bringing MarsDawn to the front.
- `--json`: print a JSON result instead of text.

Lines were added in marsdawn 0.3.0, folders and `--background` in 0.5.1, and `--wait` with the folder status in 0.5.3.

### marsdawn export

Renders a Markdown file to a paginated PDF, with the same exporter MarsDawn's own PDF export uses. It doesn't need the MarsDawn app. Relative images resolve against the input file's folder.

```
marsdawn export notes.md -o notes.pdf --theme classic --paper a4
```

- `-o, --output <path>`: where to write the PDF. Defaults to the input path with a `.pdf` extension.
- `--theme <dawn|classic|modern|vivid>`: the preview theme's light palette. Defaults to `$MARSDAWN_THEME`, then `dawn`.
- `--paper <a4|letter>`: paper size. Defaults to `a4`.
- `--breaks`: turn every newline inside a paragraph into a line break, as HackMD does. Without it, a newline between two Chinese or Japanese characters is dropped, so the lines read as one sentence.
- `--layout <document|handbook>`: the page layout. Defaults to `document`. `handbook` prints a handbook: wider margins with a binding side, each top-level heading on a new page, a contents page with page numbers, page numbers in the footer and PDF bookmarks, plus a cover when the front matter has a `title`.
- `--toc-title <text>`: the heading of the handbook's contents page. Defaults to `Contents`.
- `<!--BREAK-->` on a line of its own starts a new page, in either layout.
- `--allow-remote-images`: load images from the web while rendering. Off by default.
- `--force`: replace the output file if it already exists.
- `--json`: print a JSON result instead of text.
- A file over 16 MiB isn't exported: `export` exits 5 and writes nothing.

`--breaks` was added in marsdawn 0.7.0, `--layout` and `--toc-title` in 0.7.1, and the name `handbook` in 0.7.2. The 0.7.1 name, `manual`, still works.

### marsdawn theme

Checks a theme file (`theme.json`) and shows what it looks like, before you share it. It doesn't need the MarsDawn app. For the fields of a theme, see [Make a theme with your agent](/themes/agents/).

```
marsdawn theme validate my-theme.json
marsdawn theme css my-theme.json
marsdawn theme preview my-theme.json --appearance dark -o preview.png
```

- `validate <file>`: checks the file against every rule a MarsDawn theme must meet, with the validator the app uses. Exits 0 when the theme is valid, and 1 when it isn't, listing each problem. `--require-complete` also requires the syntax and diagram colors, which a published theme must have.
- `css <file>`: prints the CSS the preview uses for a valid theme.
- `preview <file> --appearance <light|dark> -o <out.png>`: renders a sample document with the theme to a PNG. `--width` sets its width in pixels, from 600 to 2000 (default 1200). An existing file is replaced only with `--force`.
- `--json`: print a JSON result instead of text.

The `theme` commands were added in marsdawn 0.6.1.

## The $MARSDAWN_THEME variable

When `--theme` isn't passed, `export` reads the `$MARSDAWN_THEME` environment variable. Its value must be one of `dawn`, `classic`, `modern` or `vivid`; anything else falls back to `dawn`. The CLI doesn't read the app's own theme setting, because reading another app's container can trigger a macOS privacy prompt.

## Overwriting files

`export` refuses to replace an existing output file unless you pass `--force`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | success. | With `--json`, read the one JSON line on stdout |
| `2` | input not found. | Check the path and the file name |
| `3` | MarsDawn is not installed (`open` only). | Install the app, or use `export`, which doesn't need it |
| `4` | output exists (pass `--force`). | Pass `--force` to replace it, or `-o` to write elsewhere |
| `5` | export failed. | Read `message` in the JSON result |
| `6` | this MarsDawn can't show a folder, so nothing was opened (`open` only). |  |
| `64` | usage error, including a line out of range, `--line` with more than one file or with a folder, or more than one folder. | Fix the option or value; this error is text on stderr, even with `--json` |

## --json output

On success, `marsdawn open --json` prints `ok`, `opened` (a list with each file's `path`, plus `line` when one was asked for), `app` (the app path) and, when a folder was given, `folder`. `marsdawn export --json` prints `ok`, `output`, `pages`, `theme`, `paper` and `diagramErrors`. On failure, both print `ok`, `error` and `message`.
